title: Bone-strengthening infusion for osteoporosis (zoledronic acid)
what: A medicine that strengthens the bones is given by drip into a vein. It is usually done once a year.
why: For osteoporosis, to lower the risk of fractures, when tablets are not suitable.
duration: the drip usually takes 15 to 30 minutes, and the whole visit about an hour
tell_doctor: Planned dental treatment or tooth removal

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Before the infusion, your kidney function and calcium are usually checked.

prepare.title: Water
prepare.text: Drink plenty of water before and after, unless your doctor limited it.

prepare.title: Teeth
prepare.text: It is best to have your teeth treated beforehand. Tell your dentist you are getting this medicine.

prepare.title: Vitamins
prepare.text: Take calcium and vitamin D as your doctor prescribed.

steps: The nurse checks your test results and how you feel
A catheter is placed in a vein
The medicine runs in for 15 to 30 minutes
The catheter is removed and the spot is pressed
feel: The drip itself usually does not hurt
In the first 1 to 3 days there may be fever, aches and weakness, like a cold
This reaction usually happens after the first infusion
after: For aches, you can take a fever reducer your doctor approved
The next infusion is usually in a year. The doctor will tell you the date
red_flags: Severe jaw pain or a sore in the mouth that does not heal
New pain in the thigh or groin
Rash, swelling of the face, trouble breathing: call your local emergency number

faq.q: Why do I feel like I have the flu after the infusion?
faq.a: This is a common reaction to the first dose. It usually passes in 1 to 3 days.

faq.q: Do I need to tell my dentist?
faq.a: Yes, always. Especially before a tooth is removed or implants are placed.

reminders.text: Bone infusion tomorrow. Drink more water and bring your test results.
